title: Headroom matrix — hourly glance (cluster/pool export)
content:
Context: quick exported view from the hourly headroom matrix (derived from the cluster/pool dashboards). Purpose is to surface short-term (next 24–72h) headroom pressure and candidate pools for short bursts or rebalancing. This is a working extract — includes raw rows from the dashboard and my quick notes/observations and suggested follow-ups.

Columns (export):
Timestamp, Region, Cluster, Pool, PriorityTier, TotalSlots, OccupiedSlots, ReservedSlots, AvailableHeadroom, AvgLatencyMs, P99LatencyMs, TokensPerSec, QueueDepth, BacklogJobs, SurgeHint

Sample rows (hourly, UTC):
2026-06-23T08:00Z, us-west-2, cluster-7, pool-gen-large, production, 128, 118, 8, 2, 45.2, 172, 30500, 1, 3, normal
2026-06-23T08:00Z, eu-central-1, cluster-3, pool-infer-small, standard, 64, 62, 0, 2, 38.6, 125, 11200, 2, 5, partial-burst
2026-06-23T08:00Z, ap-southeast-1, cluster-12, pool-dedicated-a, enterprise, 256, 255, 0, 1, 52.9, 310, 64000, 4, 21, sustained-burst
2026-06-23T09:00Z, us-west-2, cluster-7, pool-gen-large, production, 128, 121, 2, 5, 48.0, 190, 32000, 2, 6, microburst
2026-06-23T09:00Z, eu-central-1, cluster-5, pool-infer-medium, standard, 96, 80, 6, 10, 41.3, 140, 18400, 1, 2, low

Quick observations: 
- ap-southeast-1 / cluster-12 / pool-dedicated-a shows very low headroom (1 slot) and a growing backlog (21 jobs) over the last 4 hours; P99 latency trending up (310ms). This pool is on reserved capacity for enterprise customers — need escalation if backlog persists beyond 2 hours.
- us-west-2 cluster-7 oscillates between normal and microburst states; small headroom swing (2–5 slots) correlates with hourly traffic spikes (token bursts at :00). Consider adding burstable capacity or pre-warming a small burst pool for gen-large on the hour.
- eu-central-1 has a couple pools with partial-burst flags; these are typically caused by autoscaler thresholds being too conservative (scale-up at 70% occupancy leads to 0 headroom windows).

Derived short-term metrics (computed from the export):
- Fleet-level headroom (last hour UTC): 4.2% overall (across all clusters in the export).
- Regional headroom: us-west-2 6.8%, eu-central-1 3.1%, ap-southeast-1 0.9% (critical).
- Pools with sustained backlog (> 15 jobs) in last 6h: pool-dedicated-a (ap-southeast-1), pool-streaming-eval (us-east-1) — flagged for on-call review.

Potential root causes to triage: 
- Autoscaler sync delay (observed 60–90s) causing transient 0-headroom windows when many short-lived requests arrive simultaneously. Check autoscaler logs for scale event timing around 08:00–10:00 UTC.
- Affinity/reservation collisions: several pools show high ReservedSlots relative to TotalSlots (e.g., enterprise pools in ap-southeast-1). Are we double-reserving for Dedicated and Private customers?
- Uneven distribution of quantized workloads: gen-large workloads have longer KV cache residency which pins slots longer — causes effective headroom reduction even when occupancy looks moderate.

Immediate action items (owner assignments):
- Aisha: create quick alert (on-call) for ap-southeast-1 pool-dedicated-a when backlog >15 and headroom <=1 for >30m. Link ticket to JIRA-INFRA-9872. (ETA: 2h)
- Diego: validate autoscaler logs for eu-central-1 clusters between 07:30–09:30 UTC to measure scale latency. Add notes to the autoscaler incident board. (ETA: EOD)
- Lena: run a small canary to pre-warm a 16-slot burst pool in us-west-2 for gen-large to run between :45–:15 of each hour for the next 48h. Measure effect on P99 and backlog. (ETA: tomorrow morning)

Longer-term suggestions: 
- Revisit reserved slot policy for enterprise pools in APAC — consider a sliding reservation that frees unused reserved slots after 30m of inactivity. This would recover ephemeral headroom without impacting guaranteed capacity SLAs.
- Build a rolling 3-hour headroom forecast using historical hourly shapes + known scheduled events (deploys, customer tests) — feed into routing policy to shift low-priority requests to regions with free headroom.
- Add a derived "effective headroom" metric that discounts long-resident KV cache sessions (weights slots by recent average session length).

Notes / open questions: 
- Are the enterprise reservations for ap-southeast-1 tied to any contractually required latency window? If yes, we need a separate playbook before freeing reserved slots.
- Is the partial-burst flag coming from a single signal or multiple (queue depth vs autoscaler vs latency)? We should standardize the naming in the dashboards.

Patchy export housekeeping (meta): 
- This CSV-export was pulled from the hourly headroom API (internal). I trimmed non-essential columns (node IDs, instance serials) for readability. The original export is saved in the dashboard attachments for audit: dash-export-2026-06-23-08z.csv.
- Suggested follow-up doc: "apac-reservation-review-2026" (confluence) to collect contract details and proposed sliding reservation policy.

References & links: 
- Autoscaler trace viewer: https://traces.redwood.internal/trace?query=autoscaler+scale-event
- Current headroom dashboard (hourly): https://dashboard.redwood.internal/gpu/headroom?view=hourly
- JIRA: JIRA-INFRA-9872 (follow-up for ap-southeast-1 backlog)

Bottom line summary (TL;DR): ap-southeast-1 is the immediate pressure point (low headroom + backlog + rising P99). us-west-2 shows predictable microbursts at top of the hour and is a good candidate for small pre-warm bursts. eu-central-1 requires autoscaler latency investigation. This sheet is a working export to coordinate triage and short-term mitigation.

- [ ] Autoscaler timing audit (Diego)
- [ ] Pre-warm canary in us-west-2 (Lena)
- [ ] Add effective-headroom column to main dashboard (follow-up ticket)

End of export.
